title: When Do LLMs Apply the Wrong Law? Diagnosing LLM Failures in Temporal Legal Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2608.14610v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Legal reasoning tasks such as legal judgment prediction (LJP) require identifying the temporally correct version of the law governing a case -- a capability we term temporal applicable-law determination. However, whether large language models (LLMs) can reliably perform this task remains unexplored. In this paper, we construct a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on temporal applicable-law determination, and systematically investigate why they fail at temporal legal reasoning. Our experiments reveal four key findings. First, LLMs exhibit a strong bias toward applying the most recently enacted law, regardless of when the legally relevant facts occurred. Second, this bias does not stem from an inability to understand that laws have temporal scope, nor from a lack of knowledge about historical statutes. translated_title: 大语言模型何时适用错误的法律？诊断大语言模型在时间性法律推理中的失败
translated_abstract: 法律推理任务，如法律判决预测（LJP），要求识别适用于案件的时间上正确的法律版本——我们将这一能力称为时间性适用法律确定。然而，大语言模型（LLMs）是否能可靠地执行此任务仍未得到探索。在本文中，我们构建了一个基准来评估LLMs在时间性适用法律确定上的表现，并系统性地研究它们为何在时间性法律推理中失败。我们的实验揭示了四个关键发现。首先，LLMs表现出强烈倾向于适用最近颁布的法律，无论法律相关事实发生的时间如何。其次，这种偏差并非源于无法理解法律具有时间范围，也不是缺乏对历史法规的知识。第三，我们提供了行为证据表明，强化学习塑造的显式推理可能是一个关键机制：虽然它改善了通用推理能力，但也加剧了这种时间性偏差。
tldr: 大语言模型在时间性法律推理中倾向于错误地适用最新法律，这种偏差源于强化学习塑造的显式推理机制，而非法律知识或理解能力的缺失。
en_tdlr: LLMs tend to incorrectly apply the most recently enacted law in temporal legal reasoning, a bias driven by reinforcement-learning-shaped explicit reasoning rather than gaps in legal knowledge or comprehension.
